ranking.name: Ramada Plaza Hotel The Inn on Bourbon

text.text_excerpt: First let me say this - if you're okay with not going to sleep until Bourbon Street shuts down (midnight to 1:00 AM during the week, God only knows on the weekends), the Inn is perfect for you. Our room was basically at the corner of Bourbon and Toulouse, and wow, was it loud. You might want to look into someplace further away from the action if you like to turn in early. The cover band at Funky 544 is talented, but at 12:30 in the morning, the last thing you want to hear is another rendition of "Livin' on a Prayer" followed by choruses of "WOOOOOOO!" The good: -Spacious, clean room with a comfortable bed. Once we did fall asleep, we stayed that way. -Gorgeous bathroom with good-smelling ...

For my first time in NOLA this past October, I had to pick a hotel that was on Bourbon St. I had my mind set on that. The location of this hotel is fantastic! Right on the corner of Bourbon and Toulouse, which is dead center of Bourbon St. Locale set aside, I had more than an pleasant experience at this hotel. As a typical tourist, I bombarded the front desk and bell hops with numerous questions. Every member of personnel was very at tentative and very helpful to my questions, although I'm sure they hear the same exact questions from every tourist and are probably tired of hearing them, hahaha. Right in the middle of the French Quarter on Bourbon Street. The hotel is located on the site of the Old French Opera House, the first opera house that opened in the U.S. We got a smoking room with a balcony overlooking Toulouse St. It was perfect. In the mornings we had a relaxing coffee and at night we people-watched. There is much craziness that goes on to keep you entertained. The rooms are not completely soundproof but we were still able to fall asleep even with music pumping on Bourbon. I'm not sure if that would be possible if staying on the Bourbon street side. Hotel has an outdoor pool and a 'business room' for internet access.
